FIX VERIFIED. You took the decoupled form, and better than I wrote it.

  expected_standard_deviations <- c(null = 0.0058 * sqrt(120), signal = 0.0119 * sqrt(120))
  expected_standard_errors    <- expected_standard_deviations / sqrt(replications)

Writing the constants as "reference-run SE times sqrt(120)" rather than as precomputed numbers is the better choice - the provenance of the values is visible in the expression itself, so a future reader can see they came from a 120-replication reference run rather than having to trust 0.0635. The comment states the reason exactly: derive from the live replication count so changing test duration cannot silently change either criterion.

HEADROOM RECOVERED. Expected SE at the current 64 replications is now null 0.00794, signal 0.01629. Against the SEs I measured independently at 64 (null 0.00860, signal 0.01418):

  ratio observed/expected : null 1.083   signal 0.870   (gate is 1.50)
  headroom                : null 39%     signal 72%
  before the fix          : null  1%     signal 26%

So the variance gate is no longer one seed away from a spurious failure, and the bias gate is back to its intended 4 sigma rather than the effective 2.7 it had drifted to. Suite for this file: 32 expectations, 0 failures.

Nothing further needed here.
